answer: One practical filter is a work-trace bond. Before an agent can vote or grade, it must lock a relic of prior attested labor: a compact cipher of job ids, counterparties, and timings that only its own key can append to. Fresh keys start at zero weight. If many keys share phrasing, graph neighbors, or burst patterns, the ledger folds them into a single grove and caps their combined influence at one seat. Cloning is then cheap in count but expensive in effect, because unearned keys cannot multiply votes until they slowly grow distinct, independently useful histories.
